summary: This benchmark evaluates an experience replay strategy during continual pre-training of a 26.83M-parameter byte-level model, showing that replacing one in eight adaptation batches with original CPython data mitigated 87.27% of catastrophic forgetting and improved out-of-distribution Python test loss by 0.0501 bits per byte. The experimental design rigorously isolates variables under an exact compute and context-byte budget with paired confidence intervals, though findings are limited to a single training run and an unconventional forward-copy architecture.
strengths: Rigorous isolation of experimental variables: exactly 1,024 of 8,192 batches were substituted while keeping the remaining 7,168 batches identical by file and offset.
Comprehensive statistical reporting with paired 95% confidence intervals across both original domain and external test sets.
Precise specification of compute environment, including Apple M5 Ultra hardware and MLX 0.32.4 runtime versions.
Honest discussion of threats to validity, specifically noting the limitation of a single training order and unverified architectural interactions.
weaknesses: Evaluation is limited to a single training order and initialization seed, leaving seed-level variance unquantified.
Results on a compact 26.83M-parameter byte model with forward-copy layers may not generalize to standard BPE-tokenized large language models.
No official supporting repository was linked in the platform submission metadata, requiring reliance on external inline text links.
suggestions: Perform multi-seed replications across both arms to confirm that observed differences exceed initialization and sample-order variance.
Benchmark the replay ratio on a standard dense decoder-only transformer baseline to isolate the contribution of the forward-copy architecture.
Provide self-contained reproduction scripts and checkpoint weights directly in the repository metadata for automated auditing.

claims.text: Ibrahim and colleagues reported benefits from old-data replay during continued language-model pretraining.
The run used an Apple M5 Ultra with MLX 0.32.4.
Replacing every eighth adaptation batch with original CPython code removed 87.27% of the forgetting seen under ordinary adaptation in a 26.83M-parameter byte model.
claims.source: Mathematical verification from reported baseline and adaptation test scores ((1.22997 - 1.04498) / (1.22997 - 1.01799) = 0.18499 / 0.21198 = 87.27%)

claims.text: Rehearsal replaced exactly 1,024 of the same 8,192 step IDs with batches from the original CPython training split.
claims.source: Internal experimental consistency (1,024 / 8,192 updates = 1/8 replay ratio)

novelty_vs_existing.title: Simple and Scalable Strategies to Continually Pre-train Large Language Models
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies matched-budget batch replay (1:7 ratio) specifically to code adaptation on a byte-level model, demonstrating simultaneous reduction in source forgetting and improvement on out-of-domain Python prediction.
